Answer: B
Reason: The chest radiograph demonstrates a massive anterior mediastinal mass causing significant widening of the mediastinum, obscuration of the left heart border, and a contralateral (rightward) shift of the cardio-mediastinal structures. In a pediatric patient, this presentation is classic for T-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma (T-ALL), which typically presents as a rapidly growing thymic mass.
